channel.title: Alabama Political Reporter - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Alabama Political Reporter (alreporter.com)

item.title: Dakarai Larriett speaks out against CAW firings, removal of fluoride from water supply
item.description: The Democratic U.S. Senate candidate criticized the utility's recent mass layoffs as corporate irresponsibility and warned the policy changes threatened public health.

item.title: Gov. Ivey awards $460M to expand broadband
item.description: Investment will bring high-speed internet to 92,000 locations, strengthening economic growth, education access and long-term infrastructure across Alabama.

item.title: Alabama joins 20 other states, urging SCOTUS to review appellate voting law decision
item.description: Alabama joined a multistate effort last week, asking the Supreme Court to restore state authority over election laws in the mail-in ballot dating requirement.

item.title: Alabama bets in the shadows as lawmakers stall on sports wagering
item.description: Illegal and unregulated betting is expanding across Alabama, exposing consumers to risk while lawmakers delay action and forfeit millions in potential revenue.

item.title: UA students sue university over suspended student publications
item.description: A group of University of Alabama students filed a federal lawsuit on Wednesday, challenging the university’s suspension of two student magazines.

item.title: Mark Merrick named dean of UAB School of Health Professions
item.description: The university selected the University of Toledo dean to bring his extensive academic leadership experience to the role starting July 1.

item.title: Alabama doctors push to allow needle-free epinephrine in schools
item.description: Physicians are backing legislation to allow needle-free epinephrine options in schools, saying the added flexibility could prevent fatal allergic reactions.

item.title: Rep. Sewell blasts Treasury over delayed taxpayer refunds
item.description: Sewell demanded answers after the administration ignored a deadline to address massive wait times affecting 1.4 million taxpayers.

item.title: Sen. Britt joins bipartisan push to expand parental oversight online
item.description: Bipartisan bill would require platforms to allow parent alerts for dangerous content, targeting fentanyl sales, sextortion, cyberbullying and youth mental health risks.

item.title: U.S. Senate passes resolution honoring airmen killed in Iraq refueling plane crash
item.description: A unanimous measure remembered the six American service members who lost their lives supporting the war in Iran earlier this month.

item.title: Senate majority leader endorses Barry Moore for Senate
item.description: The endorsements of Moore’s Senate campaign by Senators John Thune and Tim Scott follow a January endorsement by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Birth centers appeal ruling in regulation battle to Alabama Supreme Court
item.description: A group of Alabama birth center is asking the state's Supreme Court to review a January decision that allowed the facilities to be regulated as hospitals.

item.title: Ivey announces 35 new Pre-K-3rd grade classrooms for 2026 school year
item.description: Governor Kay Ivey announced 35 new classrooms expanding Alabama’s P-3 early learning model, growing statewide efforts to improve literacy and early education outcomes.

item.title: Allen slams Wahl over visit to interfaith event that included Muslims
item.description: John Wahl defended his Christian faith Tuesday, calling the criticism ridiculous, while an Islamic advocacy group urged his Republican rival to visit a mosque.

item.title: Opinion | When faith becomes a weapon in Alabama politics
item.description: Wes Allen’s attack on John Wahl reveals a dangerous tactic: using faith as a political weapon rather than a guiding principle.
